articles.title: Reddit tests ads in search results
articles.summary: Reddit has begun testing a new ad format that places sponsored content directly within its search results pages, giving advertisers a way to reach users at the exact moment they're searching for information, products, or recommendations on the platform. The move comes as Reddit's internal search usage has reportedly been declining, likely due to users increasingly relying on external search engines and AI tools to surface Reddit content rather than searching within the app or site itself. By introducing ads into search, Reddit is attempting to create a new monetization opportunity tied to high-intent user behavior, since people actively searching are often further along in a decision-making or research process than those simply scrolling their feeds. This test reflects Reddit's broader push to diversify and grow its advertising business beyond traditional feed and display placements, as the company continues working to prove its value to marketers and sustain revenue growth following its 2024 public listing, even as organic search referrals to the platform face pressure from shifting search habits.
articles.li_summary: Reddit is piloting advertisements within its on-platform search results, aiming to connect brands with users during active discovery moments even as the company's internal search traffic declines.

articles.title: LinkedIn shares information on new creator insights options
articles.summary: LinkedIn has introduced updated analytics features aimed at creators, giving them deeper insight into how their content performs and where they can find new ways to monetize their presence on the platform. The refreshed insights dashboard is built to help creators better interpret post-level metrics, making it easier to understand audience engagement patterns and content reach over time. Alongside improved performance tracking, LinkedIn is positioning these updates as a gateway to additional monetization opportunities, suggesting the platform wants to give creators clearer data to inform decisions about brand partnerships, content strategy, and audience growth. While specific metrics or dashboard features weren't detailed extensively, the update reflects LinkedIn's broader push to compete with other platforms investing heavily in creator economy tools, such as YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram, all of which have rolled out similar analytics expansions recently. For marketers and professionals building personal brands on LinkedIn, this update could mean more actionable data to refine content approaches and better justify time investment in platform-specific strategies.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn rolled out updated creator analytics tools designed to help users better track post performance metrics and identify new monetization opportunities on the platform.

articles.title: Meta ends support for Quest 2 and Quest Pro
articles.summary: Meta announced it is discontinuing support for the Quest 2 and Quest Pro headsets, meaning both devices will no longer receive software updates, feature additions, or technical assistance from the company going forward. This move signals a strategic pivot as Meta concentrates its engineering and development resources on a next-generation VR headset that is expected to launch sometime next year. The decision effectively retires two of Meta's more established VR products, the budget-friendly Quest 2 and the higher-end, enterprise-oriented Quest Pro, both of which have been central to the company's mixed reality lineup for the past few years. While Meta has not detailed the full specifications or pricing for the upcoming headset, ending support for these older models suggests the new device will likely incorporate updated hardware and software architecture that diverges significantly from the current Quest ecosystem. Users still relying on Quest 2 or Quest Pro should expect their devices to function as-is without further improvements, bug fixes, or compatibility updates for newer apps and features.
articles.li_summary: Meta will stop providing software updates and support for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro headsets as it redirects resources toward a next-generation VR device slated for release next year.

articles.title: Reddit pitches its 1,300 gaming-related communities to brands
articles.summary: Reddit has launched a push to position its platform as a key advertising destination for gaming brands, highlighting a network of roughly 1,300 communities dedicated to gaming topics. The company's pitch centers on the idea that conversations within these spaces are organically created and shaped by actual players rather than brands or marketers, which it argues makes them more credible and influential than conventional advertising content. Reddit is framing this authenticity as a competitive advantage, suggesting that exposure within these player-led discussions can meaningfully increase engagement with gaming audiences and ultimately affect how those users decide what to buy, whether that's new game titles, in-game purchases, or related hardware and accessories. The move reflects a broader strategy by Reddit to court advertisers by emphasizing its niche, highly engaged communities as alternatives to more generic social feeds, betting that brands will pay a premium to reach gamers in spaces where the conversation feels unscripted and community-driven rather than sponsored.
articles.li_summary: Reddit is pitching advertisers on its 1,300 gaming-related communities, arguing that authentic player-driven discussions can boost brand engagement and sway purchasing decisions more effectively than traditional ad placements.

articles.title: X launches updated Lead Gen Ads globally
articles.summary: X has rolled out an updated version of its Lead Generation Ads product to advertisers worldwide, marking a refresh of the ad format originally designed to help brands capture user information directly within the platform. The key change highlighted in the update is a more prominent, visible call-to-action button embedded in the ad unit, intended to make it easier for users to act immediately after engaging with a post rather than navigating away to an external landing page. The goal of this redesign is to improve the conversion path from simple engagement, such as likes, comments, or impressions, into concrete lead capture for businesses running campaigns on the platform. By strengthening the visual emphasis on the CTA, X is positioning the format as a more effective tool for marketers focused on performance-driven objectives like list building, sign-ups, or inquiries, rather than purely brand awareness. The global rollout suggests X is prioritizing direct-response advertising capabilities as it continues trying to attract and retain advertiser spend on the platform.
articles.li_summary: X has globally relaunched its Lead Generation Ads format, adding a more prominent call-to-action button aimed at converting user engagement directly into qualified leads for advertisers.

articles.title: TikTok adds new brand safety resources
articles.summary: TikTok has introduced a new set of brand protection resources aimed at helping advertisers manage risk on the platform. The update centers on detection tools that flag potential copyright violations and counterfeit goods, giving brands a way to spot unauthorized use of their intellectual property or fake products being promoted under their name. This move positions TikTok alongside other major platforms that have ramped up brand safety offerings in response to advertiser concerns about where and how their content appears online. For marketing teams, these tools could reduce the manual effort needed to monitor the platform for infringing content and provide more confidence when allocating ad spend to TikTok. While specific rollout details, pricing, or availability by region were not disclosed, the addition signals TikTok's continued push to compete for advertiser trust against established players like Meta and Google, both of which already offer similar brand safety and anti-counterfeiting measures as part of their advertising ecosystems.
articles.li_summary: TikTok rolled out new brand safety tools for advertisers, adding features that help detect potential risks such as copyright infringement and counterfeit product listings on the platform.

articles.title: Meta delays commercial terms update indefinitely
articles.summary: Meta has pushed back the rollout of an upcoming update to its commercial terms of service, with no new timeline given for when the changes will take effect. The delay comes after regulators raised concerns and asked the company to provide more detailed information about what the revised terms would actually entail. Rather than move forward while those questions remain unresolved, Meta has opted to pause the update indefinitely until it can satisfy regulatory scrutiny. The specific commercial terms in question, and the business practices they would govern, have not been fully detailed publicly, but the regulatory pushback suggests concerns about transparency or potential impact on advertisers, partners, or platform users operating under commercial agreements with Meta. For marketing professionals and businesses that rely on Meta's advertising and commercial tools, this pause means current terms remain in effect for now, and any anticipated changes to contractual or commercial relationships with the company will not arrive as originally expected until regulators are satisfied with the clarifications provided.
articles.li_summary: Meta has indefinitely postponed its planned update to commercial terms of service after regulators requested more detailed information about the specific changes involved.

articles.title: Companies may need to restrict AI use to manage costs
articles.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, and Meta have collectively invested enormous sums into building out artificial intelligence infrastructure and models, yet none of these companies have reported returns that justify the scale of that spending. The gap between investment and revenue is prompting concern that businesses relying on these AI tools may eventually need to limit or ration employee access to manage ballooning costs tied to compute, API usage, and subscription fees. As model training and inference expenses continue to climb, companies building on top of these platforms face uncertainty about long-term affordability, especially if providers pass costs downstream through pricing changes or usage caps. The situation highlights a broader tension in the AI industry: massive capital expenditure from leading labs has not yet translated into profitability, leaving open questions about how sustainable current AI deployment models are for both the companies building the technology and the businesses depending on it for daily operations.
articles.li_summary: Major AI firms including Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, and Meta have poured massive capital into AI development without yet generating matching revenue, pushing companies toward usage restrictions to control costs.

articles.title: Meta updates creator assistant chatbot
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out an update to its Creator Assistant, the AI-powered chatbot built to support creators across its platforms. The refreshed tool now includes opportunity alerts, designed to flag relevant brand deals, trends, or monetization options creators might otherwise miss. It also offers enhanced content creation assistance, giving creators more robust guidance and suggestions as they plan and produce posts. Additionally, the chatbot now supports automated replies, allowing creators to handle audience engagement and common questions without manually responding to every message. Together, these additions aim to streamline the day-to-day workload for influencers and content producers who rely on Meta's platforms, reducing time spent on administrative tasks like spotting opportunities or managing comments so they can focus more on content strategy and audience growth. The update reflects Meta's ongoing push to embed AI tools deeper into its creator ecosystem, following similar moves by competitors to court influencers with smarter, more automated support features built directly into their platforms.
articles.li_summary: Meta upgraded its AI-powered Creator Assistant chatbot, adding opportunity alerts, improved content creation support, and automated reply features to help creators manage their work more efficiently.

articles.title: Threads adds more community champion badges
articles.summary: Meta's Threads app is rolling out additional community champion badges, a recognition feature designed to spotlight users who have become standout contributors within niche topical communities on the platform. These badges appear as digital display cards attached to a user's profile or posts, signaling to other members that the account plays an active, valued role in discussions around a particular subject area, whether that's sports, entertainment, hobbies, or other interest-based groups. The expansion builds on Threads' earlier efforts to foster stronger community identity and engagement by rewarding consistent, high-quality participation rather than just follower counts or likes. For marketers and brands using Threads, this signals Meta's continued push to deepen niche community formation on the app, which could make topic-specific creators and power users more influential within their subgroups and potentially valuable partners for targeted outreach or collaboration as the platform works to differentiate itself from competitors like X and Bluesky.
articles.li_summary: Threads is expanding its community champion badge program, awarding digital display cards to users who consistently drive engagement and conversation within specific topic-based subgroups on the platform.

articles.title: What Reddit’s Q3 earnings mean for marketers amid major traffic shift
articles.summary: Reddit's Q3 earnings discussion revealed a strategic pivot toward requiring users to log in to access the platform, moving away from allowing anonymous, logged-out browsing. The company frames this shift as a response to declining logged-out traffic and user loss, positioning it instead as an opportunity to build a smaller but more engaged, identifiable user base that advertisers can target more effectively. For marketers, this means Reddit's audience data will likely become richer and more reliable, since logged-in users provide better behavioral and demographic signals than anonymous visitors, improving targeting precision and measurement. However, the trade-off is a probable reduction in overall reach and top-line traffic numbers, since logged-out users—often arriving via search engines—previously inflated Reddit's scale. Marketers evaluating Reddit as an ad channel should expect a smaller but higher-intent audience, and should reassess campaign goals around engagement quality rather than raw impression volume, while watching upcoming earnings calls for concrete metrics on how this transition affects user counts, ad revenue, and advertiser demand on the platform.
articles.li_summary: Reddit is shifting toward a logged-in-only platform experience, restricting access for logged-out visitors, aiming to curb user attrition and build a more advertiser-valuable, identifiable audience base.

articles.title: X launches new bonus program for video creators
articles.summary: X has introduced a new monetization initiative aimed at growing its video content ecosystem by offering cash bonuses to a select group of invited creators. Under this reward-based program, eligible users receive direct cash incentives simply for posting videos to the platform, rather than through traditional ad-revenue sharing models. The move signals X's continued push to compete with platforms like YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels by encouraging more creators to prioritize video uploads. Details on specific payout amounts, eligibility criteria, and how creators are selected for invitations have not been fully disclosed, but the program appears designed to incentivize volume and consistency of video posting rather than performance metrics alone. This approach differs from X's existing ad-share program, which ties payouts to engagement and impressions. By directly rewarding video uploads, X may be attempting to quickly build out its video library and keep creators active on the platform amid ongoing competition for attention in the short-form and long-form video space.
articles.li_summary: X rolled out an invite-only bonus program paying selected creators cash rewards for posting videos on the platform, aiming to boost video content and engagement.

articles.title: Meta hires bipartisan political team
articles.summary: Axios reports that Meta has brought on multiple new executives who have significant connections to major figures across both the Democratic and Republican parties, signaling a deliberate push to strengthen its political relationships on both sides of the aisle. The hires reflect Meta's ongoing effort to navigate a polarized Washington landscape, where the company faces scrutiny over content moderation, antitrust concerns, and data privacy regulations regardless of which party holds power. By recruiting people with established ties to both political camps, Meta appears to be positioning itself to maintain influence and access no matter the outcome of future elections or shifts in control of Congress and the White House. The move comes as tech companies broadly continue to invest heavily in government relations and lobbying teams, aiming to shape policy debates on AI regulation, platform accountability, and competition law. Specific names and titles of the new hires were not detailed in the available reporting, but the pattern suggests a calculated bipartisan staffing strategy inside Meta's policy division.
articles.li_summary: Meta has hired several new executives with close ties to prominent Democratic and Republican political figures, according to an Axios report on the company's expanding bipartisan political operation.

articles.title: Instagram offers to pay creators for long-form content
articles.summary: Business Insider reports that Meta is courting top creators with substantial cash incentives, offering as much as $500,000 to individuals willing to publish long-form video content on its newly introduced Features product within Instagram. The offers reportedly target creators with significant followings, aiming to seed the platform with quality long-form content early on. This move signals Meta’s push to compete more directly with YouTube and TikTok, both of which have invested heavily in creator monetization programs tied to longer video formats. While exact terms, number of participating creators, and duration of these deals remain unclear, the scale of the payouts suggests Meta is prioritizing rapid content buildup over organic growth for this new offering. For marketers and brands, this development hints at a potential new advertising and partnership surface within Instagram, as well as a possible shift in creator strategy toward longer, more in-depth content rather than short clips, which could reshape influencer campaign planning in the months ahead.
articles.li_summary: Instagram, per Business Insider, is dangling payouts of up to $500,000 to select creators who post long-form video content to Meta’s newly launched Features product.

articles.title: Reddit looks to move toward a logged-in experience
articles.summary: Reddit's latest quarterly results reveal a mixed picture that's pushing the company to rethink how people access its platform. In Q3, U.S. weekly active unique visitors fell, and traffic coming from search engines—historically a major discovery channel for Reddit threads—saw a significant decline, likely tied to changes in how Google and other search platforms surface content. Despite these usage pressures, Reddit's revenue grew by more than 50% compared to the same period last year, showing that monetization efforts, including advertising and data-licensing deals, are still paying off even as raw traffic softens. In response, Reddit executives are signaling a strategic pivot: encouraging more visitors to log in rather than browse anonymously or arrive via search snippets. articles.li_summary: Reddit is shifting strategy toward a logged-in user experience after its Q3 report showed U.S. weekly active users declining and search-referral traffic dropping sharply, even though total revenue still climbed more than 50% year-over-year.

articles.title: Sociable: Meta says its expanded processing capacity is driving ad results
articles.summary: Meta detailed how AI-driven upgrades to its ad delivery infrastructure are boosting advertiser performance, stating that in Q2 2026 improvements to its ads ranking system increased Facebook ad clicks by 8.3% and conversions by 15.7%. Key drivers include an upgraded Andromeda system, which now matches a wider range of products to individual user interests; an expanded Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM) that processes more engagement signals per user; and GenRecs, which predicts relevant ads even for new campaigns with little engagement history. In Q3, Andromeda alone added 1.4% more Facebook conversions, while newly launched generative retrieval in Facebook Feed drove nearly a 2% conversion increase in targeted segments. Separately, Meta said its AI business assistant, now rolling out more broadly, is generating 5% more conversions at the same ad spend. Partnership ads, which let brands run campaigns alongside creators, grew over 97% year-over-year in Q3 and now exceed a $15 billion annual revenue run-rate. Meta also plans to add checkout functionality to AI agents like Muse, enabling in-stream purchases, as expanding data center capacity continues fueling these ad-targeting gains.
articles.li_summary: Meta reported that Q2 2026 upgrades to its Andromeda, GEM, and GenRecs ad-ranking systems lifted Facebook ad clicks 8.3% and conversions 15.7%, while partnership ads revenue surpassed a $15 billion annual run-rate.

articles.title: Disney plans TikTok Shop holiday experience with over 20 brands
articles.summary: Disney is launching its first-ever Super Brand Day on TikTok Shop, running Nov. 4-10, marking a major push into social commerce as part of its "Make the Holidays Magic" holiday campaign. The event will combine Disney Store merchandise with collections from more than 20 participating brands, including Old Navy, Crocs, Touchland, ColourPop, Corkcicle, Kyte Baby, FHI Heat, Girls Crew and PopSockets, all offering Disney, Pixar, Marvel or Star Wars-themed products across categories like toys, beauty, home and fashion. Two items, a "Darth on a Hearth" collectible and a Loungefly holiday mini backpack, will be sold exclusively on Disney Store's TikTok Shop before later appearing on Disney's own website. The campaign will be supported by paid media and creator content. This follows Disney's August content-sharing partnership with TikTok and comes as TikTok Shop's U.S. sales are projected to grow 48% next year to $23.4 billion, according to Emarketer, with GlobalData research showing 67% of U.S. shoppers, and 82% of those aged 18-24, trust brands more when discovered through TikTok Shop versus other platforms.
articles.li_summary: Disney will host its first TikTok Shop Super Brand Day from Nov. 4-10, uniting Disney Store products with over 20 partner brands like Old Navy, Crocs and ColourPop, plus platform-exclusive holiday items, as part of its "Make the Holidays Magic" campaign.

articles.title: What marketers should know about the legal risks of algorithmic pricing
articles.summary: Legal expert Laura Brett of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett outlines mounting legal risks for marketers using algorithmic pricing, which sets different prices for different customers based on data like browsing history, location, or loyalty status. New York Governor Kathy Hochul must decide by Dec. 31 whether to sign the One Fair Price Act, a broad ban on individualized pricing. This follows a December 2025 controversy where Consumer Reports found Instacart charging some shoppers up to 23% more for identical items, prompting New York Attorney General Letitia James to demand pricing records even after Instacart halted the practice. Brett distinguishes "dynamic pricing" (same price shown to everyone, varying by time or demand) from riskier "surveillance" or "personalized pricing" (different prices per customer). Over 20 states have pending bills, the FTC has issued a draft policy statement on the issue, and a House Oversight probe has sought records from Uber and Lyft. New Jersey allows private lawsuits with treble damages. Brett advises marketers to audit data inputs, map pricing practices across jurisdictions, and involve legal counsel early, since transparent, criteria-based loyalty discounts carry lower risk than device- or location-based pricing or shared third-party pricing tools that could suggest competitor coordination.
articles.li_summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul faces a Dec. 31 deadline to sign or veto the One Fair Price Act, a sweeping ban on individualized algorithmic pricing, as regulators nationwide intensify scrutiny of practices like Instacart's 23%-higher pricing for some shoppers.

articles.title: Pinterest reports solid user growth in Q3
articles.summary: Pinterest's Q3 2026 earnings, released Oct. 29, revealed strong platform momentum, with monthly active users reaching 661 million, a gain of 21 million from the previous quarter. European user growth rebounded after a year of stagnation and decline, while 17 million new users came from "Rest of World" markets outside the U.S. and Europe, which still generate less revenue per user. Gen Z now makes up 57% of Pinterest's audience, and engagement is climbing in the U.S. and Canada across search, board creation, and outbound clicks. Revenue hit $1.17 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with U.S. and Canada revenue growing 14%, though European regulatory changes affecting cross-border selling dampened international gains. Pinterest rolled out its programmatic ad-buying tool globally and launched visual search ads last month, letting brands appear in search results and Pin close-ups, capitalizing on more than 80 billion monthly searches. The company is also expanding creator monetization, including sponsored creator Pins and a Roku TV show, while continuing to face scrutiny over rising AI-generated content in Pins.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest's Q3 2026 results show 661 million monthly active users, up 21 million from Q2, with revenue climbing 12% year-over-year to $1.17 billion.

articles.title: YouTube subscriptions are rising as more users turn to CTV
articles.summary: Alphabet's Q3 2026 earnings show YouTube's advertising growth cooling to 9% year-over-year ($11.2 billion), down from 13% in Q2, even as subscription revenue accelerates, helping drive an 11% rise in Google's overall subscription income. YouTube Music and Premium subscribers reached 150 million, up from the 100 million milestone hit in early 2024, with connected TV viewing cited as a key driver since Nielsen's August 2026 Gauge report named YouTube the top U.S. streaming platform. Google Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler noted that Living Room, YouTube's CTV experience, now generates over a third of total ad revenue. The platform also reported over three million creators in its partner program and 1.3 million channels using its shopping tools, alongside a new Amazon affiliate feature letting U.S. creators tag products in videos and Shorts. On AI, Schindler highlighted new generative tools in YouTube Studio and Shorts, including a "reimagine" remix feature and conversational editing assistants, with a recent YouTube survey finding 61% of recent uploaders interested in using AI to insert themselves into content.
articles.li_summary: YouTube's Q3 2026 ad revenue hit $11.2 billion (up 9% year over year, slower than Q2's 13%), while Premium and Music subscriptions climbed to 150 million, up from 100 million in early 2024.

articles.title: Threads tests smaller group sharing option
articles.summary: Threads, Meta's text-based app, is piloting a new feature called Threads Friends that mirrors Instagram's Close Friends tool, letting users build a private sub-group of up to 50 connections to share posts with instead of broadcasting to their entire audience. Users can create this curated list and choose to post updates visible only to that group rather than all followers. People included on a Threads Friends list will see a label indicating their membership, and if they like or reply to a post, other members of that same list can see their username and interaction. Threads confirmed the test is currently limited to users in Ireland, Italy, and Japan, though anyone globally can be added to a Friends list regardless of location. The move reflects a broader industry shift away from public, one-to-many posting toward smaller, more private group sharing, and could give Threads a fresh mechanism to boost engagement by encouraging more intimate, frequent posting among trusted connections rather than general public broadcasts.
articles.li_summary: Threads is testing "Threads Friends," a Close Friends-style feature letting users share posts with a curated list of up to 50 connections, currently piloting in Ireland, Italy, and Japan.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul must decide by December 31 whether to sign the One Fair Price Act, a broad ban on individualized pricing across most industries, reflecting a surge of similar bills pending in more than 20 states. A House Oversight committee has also sought records from Uber and Lyft, while the FTC has drafted guidance on when personalized pricing becomes deceptive or unfair. States vary widely, some banning the practice in grocery and retail, others requiring disclosures like New York's algorithm-pricing notices, with New Jersey allowing private lawsuits and treble damages. articles.title: What influencer fatigue says about creator-driven marketing’s next phase
articles.summary: A Nantucket artisan shop's "no influencers" sign went viral this July, sparking debate over whether influencer culture has worn out its welcome, and reigniting discussion of so-called "influencer fatigue." Yet data suggests the channel remains strong: 72% of young consumers follow influencers, 58% have bought products based on creator endorsements, and nearly 80% of brands work with one to ten influencers at a time, according to the Association of National Advertisers, which projects U.S. creator-economy ad spend will hit $43.9 billion by 2026. Over 80% of marketers plan to boost influencer budgets within a year, per Sprout Social, even as costs rise through pricier PR packages, brand trips and fees, plus new tools like Meta's creator-matching suite. More than half of creators with 500,000-plus followers report friction between brand demands and audience expectations. Whisker CMO Hew Loyd, who manages influencer relationships in-house (done by only 16% of marketers), says fatigue is real in person but more nuanced online, as brands shift toward niche-fit over follower count, now ranked the least important selection factor.

articles.title: Reddit introduces For You feed
articles.summary: Reddit is introducing a new For You feed powered by algorithmic recommendations, designed to help users discover new subreddits and discussions beyond the communities they've already joined. This feed will sit alongside the existing Following feed, which shows updates from communities users already follow, giving people a clearer split between discovery and catch-up browsing. Notably, For You has been placed in the primary tab position as Reddit pushes discovery, though it won't be the default view—the app will instead open to whichever feed a user last viewed. Reddit says the change uses its engagement and audience data to predict content users might find interesting, framing it as part of ongoing experiments to make the platform more valuable, with future plans including more navigation options and controls like hiding posts or flagging unwanted content. The rollout will happen globally over the coming weeks. The move comes amid broader industry debate over algorithmic feeds' risks and benefits, and growing calls for platforms to offer non-algorithmic, chronological feed opt-outs.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse AI agents are now available to users in Singapore
articles.summary: Meta has launched its Muse AI agent in Singapore, marking the first expansion of the tool into Southeast Asia after its U.S. and Canada debut last month, where it hit 10 million downloads within its first 30 days. In Singapore, Muse connects to personal apps like Gmail, Google Calendar and Instagram to manage email, scheduling and saved content, while also linking to local partners including Shopee, Lazada, Grab, GrabMart, Grab Dine Out, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, Klook, Trip.com and ShopBack to help users compare prices, book travel, order food and earn cashback. The move follows Zuckerberg's comments on Meta's Q3 earnings call that shopping is Muse's top use case, with over 25% of users seeking deals or making purchases averaging more than $200 each — a trend Meta likely hopes to amplify in Singapore's e-commerce-heavy market. The expansion reflects Meta's broader push to embed AI into daily routines as it tries to justify AI spending that could eventually top $1 trillion, with Muse positioned as a potential key driver toward profitability.
articles.li_summary: Meta expanded its Muse AI assistant to Singapore, its first Southeast Asia launch, adding local app integrations with Shopee, Grab, Lazada, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, Klook, Trip.com and ShopBack for shopping, dining and travel tasks.
